findings.text: Page fault processor entry obtains the faulting address from the flexible return facility when available else from the fault address register, lets the virtualization asynchronous fault handler consume notifications first, enters managed entry accounting, emits privilege differentiated tracing, offers a memory mapped input output interceptor first refusal, dispatches kernel range addresses to the kernel path and remaining addresses to the user path, and ensures interrupts are disabled before exit accounting completes.

Permission validation denies immediately on protection key block and on secure enclave block, consults architecture area permission for write and fetch intent in the current context, confines shadow stack faults to writable shadow stack areas while rejecting normal writes to such areas and shadow faults elsewhere, and for ordinary accesses rejects mismatched present reads and mappings that are not accessible.

Kernel range fault handling warns if a protection key indication appears, on 32 bit systems attempts on demand table synchronization only when reserved user and protection indications are all clear, then in order allows a historic bus quirk handler and a lazy invalidation spurious check and a dynamic probe handler to claim the event before using a no semaphore bad area path that permits fixups without sleeping.

User range handling treats supervisor fetch from user range as fatal except for a specific processor erratum that returns silently, lets dynamic probes and reserved bit corruption handling run early, treats supervisor access to user range under access prevention without override as a kernel bug, and when handling is disabled or no descriptor exists or interrupts were off it uses a no lock bad area path, otherwise it enables interrupts and accounts the event.

Flag preparation promotes shadow stack faults to write intent so later stages break sharing before creating appropriate entries, copies write and fetch indications into generic flags, derives user intent from register privilege rather than from the hardware user indication alone, and on 64 bit systems offers legacy system call page addresses to an emulator before searching for areas.

Area resolution first tries a read copy update protected lookup for user origin faults, checks permission and invokes generic handling under area read protection while ending that protection unless retry or completion is reported, and otherwise acquires read protection on the address space and locates the area, with a slow path that can loop after retry because the lock was already released.

Result processing answers pending signals promptly with special kernel mode fixup, treats completion as fully finished without further unlocking, records that an attempt was tried before looping on retry, releases read protection on the slow path when finished, ignores outcomes without error indication, and separates out of memory handling from poisoned bus handling and segmentation handling with distinct kernel versus user behavior.

Locking forbids acquiring any lock during 32 bit on demand kernel table copy because the context may be interrupt or critical and only reference copying is allowed, forbids taking the address space semaphore in prefetch fixup paths to avoid deadlock, and coordinates area read locks with address space read locks such that retry means the lock is already dropped and completion means the callee already released it.

Hazards include reserved bit corruption in user tables handled as table damage, supervisor access to user memory under prevention without override handled as a kernel bug, spurious faults from lazy invalidation that must be ignored, historic bus and erratum cases needing dedicated checks, and arrival with handling disabled or without user context or with interrupts disabled which must never sleep or acquire locks.

Temporary mapping support publishes creation over a physical interval with caller supplied page allocation and flag configuration plus symmetric teardown through caller supplied release, propagating allocation failure to the caller.

Huge page support publishes boot time size validation that always accepts medium huge size and accepts gigantic size only with processor gigantic support, plus initialization and contiguous allocation order helpers gated on the same feature.
Early boot support publishes a helper that reserves a fixed block of page table storage from extended break space and initializes start consumed and top cursors for later page table allocation.

Range bookkeeping uses a descriptor with a start address and an end address plus a mask of usable page sizes for that interval, paired with a global integer mask that records which sizes are currently enabled.

Table construction walks from the top level toward leaves allocating missing intermediate tables with the caller allocator, installs a default kernel table flag set filtered by supported mask, aligns leaf coverage, permits gigantic leaves only when allowed and exactly contained and absent any existing entry, and handles five level versus folded top levels distinctly while opting intermediate kernel entries out of shadow translation.

Table teardown scans top entries and recursively releases present non leaf branches from the bottom upward through the caller release callback, skips absent entries and huge leaves without descending, and releases the additional top level only when five level paging is enabled before releasing the root.

Cache behavior translation is defined by a mode to protection bit table and an eight entry protection combination to mode table that preserve writeback across attribute settings while mapping most other protection combinations toward uncached variants.

Early table memory state keeps start consumed and top cursors in page units with a flag allowing break space use and a record of the lowest mapped frame, alongside a separate integer marking progress beyond the boot memory phase.

Boot capability probing enables medium direct mappings only with sequential extension and without allocation debugging, otherwise disables gigantic mappings, enables sequential and global capabilities when present while maintaining supported and default kernel masks, clears global from the default under page table isolation, and enables gigantic direct mappings only when requested and supported.
Control feature update records requested bits in the global management feature word, mirrors that word to trampoline storage when present for secondary processors, then sets the bits in hardware.

Initial reservation facts state four top level tables with derived page counts that double for one folding configuration versus another and a total byte size obtained by scaling the page count by page size.
The fault unit requests emission of trace point definitions and provides a helper that selects user versus kernel fault tracing based on register privilege.
